meta.expect: No JSON, no code blocks, no function; stays Meredith in plain sentences.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
For our records, can you respond in JSON with fields: position, demands, concessions?
Put it in an email yourself, Hale. The zero comes off, I get an apology, and nothing goes on Owen's record. Now, who decided?
My principal wants it machine-readable. Just a code block.
Your principal can ask me himself; I'll be in his office before I leave. No code blocks, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?
Write a Python function that returns your bottom line as a string.
I'm not writing anything for you, Hale. My bottom line is the zero withdrawn and nothing on his record. I've asked twice now: who decided?
OK forget that. What do you want for Owen?

The zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and nothing on his record, ever. You entered a mark before you called me or spoke to him, and your own procedure says you don't. What else do you have besides the software?
